claims.text: Jev MCP gives agents tools for evidence verification, classification, reranking, extraction and patch review.

evidence.quote:
Give your agent twelve judgment tools:

- `jev_verify` checks claims against evidence.
- `jev_screen` judges content before it enters context.
- `jev_noul` returns a calibrated probability for a stated proposition.
- `jev_find` picks the best candidate by meaning.
- `jev_rerank` scores and sorts every candidate.
- `jev_classify` batch-assigns items to classes.
- `jev_decide` settles bounded alternatives.
- `jev_compare` judges how two passages relate.
- `jev_extract` pulls field values with regex plus judgment.
- `jev_audit` audits extracted values against their source before they are trusted.
- `jev_review` scores a proposed diff before the task is called done.
- `jev_gate` reviews a patch and verifies completion claims in one call.

claims.text: Tools translate these jobs into Jev Choice, Score or Noul questions; extraction selects regex-found values and application code maps answers to actions.

evidence.quote: Jev is TypeSafe's System One model: it returns typed answers with calibrated probability distributions, not generated text. A verify call is a Choice over supports / contradicts / says_nothing, so you see the whole distribution, not one label. A screen call is a set of yes/no probabilities. A find call is a Choice over your candidate ids plus an existence check. A rerank call is one yes/no relevance question per candidate. A compare call is a Choice over three relations, repeated independently per aspect. An extract call is a Choice over the candidates your regex already found, so the model picks a value but never writes one. A review call is four Score rubrics plus one safe-to-apply probability; a gate adds one Choice per completion claim, judged from evidence only. Code maps the answers to verdicts and actions; policy stays with you.

claims.text: Register npx -y @jkudish/jev-mcp in an MCP client using Node.js 22 or newer and a configured Jev provider key.

evidence.quote:
## Install

Requires Node.js 22 or newer and an API key for a Jev provider ([TypeSafe direct](https://console.typesafe.ai/settings/keys) is the default; alternatives are listed under [Configuration](#configuration)).

### Let an agent install it for you

Paste this into your coding agent:

```text
Install the Jev MCP server for me. The package is @jkudish/jev-mcp on npm and the server
command is `npx -y @jkudish/jev-mcp`; register it as an MCP server with your client. Check whether
TYPESAFE_API_KEY is already set in the server environment; if not, walk me through setting it up without
pasting the key into the chat (I can create one at console.typesafe.ai/settings/keys). When it's
registered, ask if I'd like to try a claim verification, and when we do, show me the verdicts and cost.
Full instructions: https://github.com/jkudish/jev-mcp#readme
```

From npm:

```bash
npx -y @jkudish/jev-mcp
```

claims.text: Choice and Score confidence measures concentration, not correctness. Default thresholds need task-specific tuning, and policy remains in the caller’s code.

evidence.quote:
For Choice and Score, `confidence` measures how peaked the option probabilities are, scaled from 0 for a uniform distribution to 1 for all probability on one option; it is not the probability the answer is correct, so tune thresholds against observed outcomes.

## Limits and tuning

- Thresholds (`auto_accept`, `block_at`, `review_at`, exists cutoffs) are starting points from the TypeSafe cookbooks. Tune them against your own data before you enforce them. See [how TypeSafe reports confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md).
- Jev is calibrated, not infallible. Typed output guarantees the interface, not the truth. Keep policy in code and escalate low-confidence results to a person or a bigger model.
- Every result that calls the model includes token usage, so you can see what each judgment costs. A `jev_extract` call where no field reaches the model reports `usage: null`.

tr.summary: Jev MCP ajanlara kanıt doğrulama, sınıflandırma, yeniden sıralama, çıkarma ve yama inceleme araçları sunar. Node.js 22 veya üstü ve Jev sağlayıcı anahtarıyla npx -y @jkudish/jev-mcp komutunu MCP istemcisine kaydedin.

sections.heading: Ne işe yarar
sections.text: Jev MCP ajanlara kanıt doğrulama, sınıflandırma, yeniden sıralama, çıkarma ve yama inceleme araçları sunar.

sections.heading: Jev’in rolü
sections.text: İşler Choice, Score veya Noul sorularına çevrilir; çıkarma regex ile bulunan değerleri seçer, uygulama kodu yanıtları eylemlere dönüştürür.

sections.heading: Başlangıç
sections.text: Node.js 22 veya üstü ve Jev sağlayıcı anahtarıyla npx -y @jkudish/jev-mcp komutunu MCP istemcisine kaydedin.

sections.heading: Kapsam ve sınırlar
sections.text: Choice ve Score güveni doğruluğu değil yoğunlaşmayı ölçer. Eşikleri kendi verinize uyarlayın; politika çağıran kodda kalmalıdır.

it.title: jev-mcp — Giudizi tipizzati Jev come strumenti MCP
it.h1: jev-mcp — Giudizi tipizzati Jev come strumenti MCP
it.description: jev-mcp: Verifica, classificazione, riordino e giudizi sulle patch Jev via MCP; l’agente mantiene le regole d’azione.
it.summary: Jev MCP offre agli agenti verifica delle prove, classificazione, riordino, estrazione e revisione delle patch. Registra npx -y @jkudish/jev-mcp in un client MCP con Node.js 22 o successivo e una chiave del fornitore Jev.

sections.heading: A cosa serve
sections.text: Jev MCP offre agli agenti verifica delle prove, classificazione, riordino, estrazione e revisione delle patch.

sections.heading: Ruolo di Jev
sections.text: Traduce i compiti in Choice, Score o Noul; l’estrazione sceglie valori trovati da regex e il codice associa risposte e azioni.

sections.heading: Come iniziare
sections.text: Registra npx -y @jkudish/jev-mcp in un client MCP con Node.js 22 o successivo e una chiave del fornitore Jev.

sections.heading: Ambito e limiti
sections.text: La confidenza Choice e Score misura concentrazione, non correttezza. Adatta le soglie ai tuoi dati e mantieni le regole nel codice chiamante.
